figures.caption: Figure 5. Through-thickness variation in mean fiber orientation for (a) 18 µm and (b) 23 µm fiber webs with initial orientation distributions of 10° and 30°. Ø denotes the fiber diameter. The localization of this response is consistent with the prescribed penetration depth and the distribution of barbs along the needle. Near the upper surface, the needle tip initially displaces fibers before the barb-bearing region enters the batt, whereas fibers near the lower surface experience fewer barb interactions as the needle approaches its prescribed penetration depth. The barb-bearing region consequently interacts most extensively with fibers within the batt interior. Precursor architecture therefore changes the magnitude of reorientation substantially while having a smaller influence on the through-thickness location at which the maximum response occurs under the identical punching conditions

figures.caption: Figure 8. Fiber–barb engagement during needle penetration for (a) barb with no kick-up (b) barb with kick-up distance 0.3Øneedle. The simulation frames showing the influence of barb kick-up on fiber engagement is illustrated for qualitative analysis in Figure 8. For visualization, fibers engaged by the barb are shown while surrounding fibers are omitted. The trajectories can be seen in Video S5 available in the Supporting Information. In the absence of barb kick-up, only limited barb–fiber engagement occurs because the barb remains largely contained within the needle profile. Increasing the kick-up to 30% exposes a greater portion of the barb to the surrounding network, resulting in visibly greater fiber capture and downward transport along the penetration trajectory.
